spans.s: in comp. for स्थेमन्.
स्थेम—भाज् mfn. firm, strong, Śiś.
firmness, stability, TS.; Br.; Kāṭh.
continuance, duration (˚म्ना ind. ‘perseveringly’), HYog.
the state of standing or stopping still, rest, Naiṣ.
, स्थैर्य &c. See p. 1265.
(˚म्ना), ind., ‘perseveringly’
mf(आ)n. to be stationed or fixed or settled &c.
placed (as water in a jar), ŚāṅkhGṛ.
to be stood still, R.
(it is) to be stood firm (in battle), BhP.
(it is) to be stayed or remained in (loc.), R.; Hariv. &c.
(attention) is to be fixed on (loc.), MBh.; R. &c.
(it is) to be behaved or acted or proceeded (with instr. ind.p. or adv.), Hariv.; Bhartṛ.; Rājat.
a person chosen to settle a dispute between two parties, an arbitrator, umpire, judge, Rājat.; Hit.
a domestic priest, L.
(compar. of स्थिर) firmer, stronger, more important or worthy of consideration, very firm or strong, TS. &c.
very continuous or constant, Rājat.
very resolute, Sāh.
(स्थेयी for स्थेय, m.) made an arbitrator or umpire or judge, Kathās.
(superl. of स्थिर) most fixed, very firm or strong or durable, Pāṇ. vi, 4, 157.
